title: 2018 AMC 8 Problem 20
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) a point \(E\) is on \(\overline{AB}\) with \(AE=1\) and \(EB=2.\) Point \(D\) is on \(\overline{AC}\) so that \(\overline{DE} \parallel \overline{BC}\) and point \(F\) is on \(\overline{BC}\) so that \(\overline{EF} \parallel \overline{AC}.\) What is the ratio of the area of \(CDEF\) to the area of \(\triangle ABC?\)

solutions.text:
Let the area of \(\triangle ABC\) be equal to \(t.\) Since \(DE \parallel BC\) and \(FE \parallel CA ,\) we can deduce that \[ADE \sim ABC\] and \[EFB \sim ABC. \] Since \(AE = \dfrac{AB}3,\) the area of \(ADE\) is equal to \(\left(\dfrac13\right)^2 t = \dfrac{t}{9} .\) Since \(EB = \dfrac{2AB}3,\) the area of \(EFB\) is equal to \(\left(\dfrac23\right)^2 t = \dfrac{4}{9}t .\) Finally, to find the area of \(CDEF,\) we take the area of \(ABC =t\) and subtract the areas of \(ADE \) and \(EFB.\) This is equivalent to the expression \[t- \frac{t}{9} - \frac{4t}{9} = \frac{4t}{9} .\] Therefore, the ratio of the area of \(CDEF\) and \(ABC \) is \(\dfrac{\left(\dfrac{4t}{9}\right)}{t} = \dfrac{4}{9} .\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Use similarity from the two parallel-line conditions.
Compare the areas of the two small corner triangles to the area of \(\triangle ABC\).
